About Us
Co-Educational Secondary School For 11-18 Year Olds
From Seed to Summit
Welcome to Hammersmith Academy – a school founded on the belief that every young person deserves a transformational education.
Our mission is simple and ambitious: Hammersmith Academy provides the challenge, opportunity and community that allows each student to find their path to success in the real world.
Since opening in 2011, we have helped thousands of young people achieve academic success, secure places at leading universities, progress onto prestigious degree apprenticeships, and build fulfilling careers across a wide range of professions. While much has changed over the years, our commitment to ensuring every student achieves their full potential remains constant.
At Hammersmith Academy, students benefit from expert teaching, high expectations and a curriculum designed to develop both knowledge and character. We challenge students to think deeply, work hard and aim high, while providing the support and guidance they need to succeed.
What makes our Academy distinctive is the breadth of opportunities available beyond the classroom. Through exceptional partnerships with organisations including St Paul’s School, St Paul’s Girls’ School, universities, cultural institutions and leading employers, students gain experiences that broaden horizons, raise aspirations and prepare them for life beyond school.
We are equally proud of the community we have built. Ours is a school where students feel known, supported and inspired to contribute positively to the world around them. Guided by our values of Responsibility, Resilience, Resourcefulness and Respect, students develop the confidence, independence and character needed to thrive in modern society.
Whether your child joins us in Year 7 or Sixth Form, they will become part of an ambitious, inclusive and aspirational community that is committed to helping them achieve real world success.
I hope this website gives you a sense of what makes Hammersmith Academy such a special place to learn, grow and succeed. We look forward to welcoming you to our Academy.
Gary KynastonHeadteacher
Responsibility, Resilience, Resourcefulness, Respect
At Hammersmith Academy, education is more than exam results, it is about character, confidence and the skills that shape a fulfilling life. We combine academic challenge with exceptional pastoral support, creating an environment where every student feels known, supported and empowered.
Ranked within the top 15% for student progress and top 25% of schools nationally for GCSE results, we help students achieve their personal best, from confident learners to future leaders.
Our ethos is defined by four core values: Responsibility • Resilience • Resourcefulness • Respect. These principles guide how we learn, behave, and grow as a community.
Academic Excellence, Enriched by Opportunity
Our knowledge-rich curriculum is taught by passionate subject specialists who set high expectations and nurture intellectual curiosity. What sets us apart is the breadth and depth of real world opportunities woven into school life.
Through our unique private school partnerships with St Paul’s School, St Paul’s Girls’ School, and our sponsors The Mercers’ Company and The Worshipful Company of Information Technologists, students access masterclasses, academic stretch, cultural experiences, and expert-led enrichment rarely found in the state sector.
We are uniquely enriched by an outstanding network of partnerships that broaden horizons and open doors for our students. Our cultural and industry partners — including Kensington Palace, the Design Museum, the Old Vic, RHS, Royal College of Music, National Geographic, the British Exploring Society and Motorsport UK — provide extraordinary real-world experiences that develop confidence, cultural capital and professional awareness. These partnerships ensure every student benefits from opportunities far beyond the traditional classroom.
These experiences open minds, raise aspirations, and ensure students leave us confident in any environment – academically, socially and professionally.

pageCache.pageTitle: Students Launch Natural History GCSE with Education Secretary - Hammersmith Academy
pageCache.text:
Students Launch Natural History GCSE with Education Secretary
Students from Hammersmith Academy were invited to the Natural History Museum on Thursday 11th June 2026 to take part in the national launch of the Government’s proposed new Natural History GCSE, giving them a unique opportunity to contribute to discussions about the future of environmental and science education.
The event, hosted by the Natural History Museum in partnership with the Department for Education, marked the launch of a national consultation on the proposed qualification. The new GCSE aims to help young people develop a deeper understanding of the natural world while building the knowledge, skills and practical experiences needed for the careers of the future.
As part of the event, students took part in hands-on science activities in the Museum’s Nature Activity Centre and had the opportunity to engage with leading figures from the worlds of education, science and conservation. Education Secretary Bridget Phillipson met with students to discuss the role of the new qualification and how it will help future generations understand and care for the world around them.
The proposed qualification places a strong emphasis on learning beyond the classroom, with practical fieldwork forming a central part of the course. Students would explore habitats including woodlands, freshwater environments, grasslands, farmland and urban ecosystems, while developing scientific skills and a deeper understanding of biodiversity, conservation and climate change.
Hammersmith Academy students also participated in an online discussion with renowned naturalist, explorer, presenter and author Steve Backshall. During the session, he spoke about the importance of helping young people develop a genuine connection with nature and how hands-on experiences can inspire curiosity, scientific thinking and a lifelong appreciation of the natural world.
Launching the consultation, Bridget Phillipson highlighted the importance of ensuring young people develop the skills needed for the jobs of tomorrow, noting that careers are increasingly being shaped by science, technology and environmental change.
The proposed GCSE is intended to equip students with the knowledge, skills and fieldwork experience needed to access opportunities in some of the UK’s fastest-growing sectors.
Gary Kynaston, Headteacher, said:
“At Hammersmith Academy, we are committed to ensuring our students are at the forefront of education and have opportunities to contribute to conversations that shape their futures. This was a unique opportunity for our students to engage with leading figures in education, science and conservation, while gaining first-hand insight into a proposed qualification that could inspire the next generation of environmental scientists and conservationists.”

Work Experience
Building Confidence for the Real World
At Hammersmith Academy, we know that some of the most powerful lessons happen outside the classroom.
Work experience gives students their first real taste of the professional world — a moment when learning, independence, and ambition come together.
For many, it’s the first time they see how what they’ve learned in school connects with the real world: stepping into an office, shadowing a professional, collaborating on a project, or simply learning the importance of timekeeping and teamwork.
These experiences spark self-belief and open new possibilities, shaping the aspirations that drive our students toward real world success.
Every Year 10 student takes part in a structured one-week work experience placement, a key milestone in their development.
This placement helps students build confidence, gain independence, and develop essential skills such as:
Our dedicated Careers Team ensures every placement is safe, purposeful, and matched to students’ interests — whether in architecture, law, retail, education, construction, engineering, finance, horticulture, medicine, dentistry, or sport (including QPR).
These experiences help students see what’s possible and begin to imagine the futures they want to build.
In the Sixth Form, work experience becomes a test of initiative and ambition.
Students are encouraged to take the lead — researching roles, contacting employers, and proactively seeking opportunities that complement their university or apprenticeship aspirations.
Our Careers Team supports each student with advice, contacts, and access to a vast network of organisations. With our guidance, Sixth Formers have found placements in almost every sector imaginable — from medicine and media to architecture, engineering, and business.
This approach fosters independence, determination, and the professional mindset universities and employers value most.
Communication and teamwork
Problem-solving and time management
Professional conduct and responsibility
Resilience in new and unfamiliar environments
Real Partnerships, Real Impact
We work closely with a wide range of employers — from creative industries and professional services to healthcare, sport, and technology — giving students access to workplaces that reflect London’s incredible diversity.
Students gain authentic, hands-on experience in environments that challenge them to think critically, communicate effectively, and adapt quickly — the skills that define future leaders.
A Community That Opens Doors
Our vibrant alumni network also plays an important role in the programme. Many of our former students now return to offer placements, share their experiences, and inspire the next generation.
By connecting with those who have walked the same corridors and sat in the same classrooms, our students gain real insight into the journey from school to career success.
Setting the Foundation for the Future
By the end of the programme, students return to the Academy with more than just experience — they return with confidence, purpose, and a clearer vision for what comes next.
For some, work experience affirms their goals; for others, it reveals new possibilities they never considered.
Whatever the path, every placement marks the start of something bigger: a young person taking their first confident step into the world of work.

Student Leaders
Student Leadership & Citizenship
Developing Confident Leaders and Budding Citizens
Our Junior Leadership Team (JLT) is a central part of Academy life, giving students the opportunity to lead, influence, and shape the school community.
JLT members represent the student voice, working closely with staff to strengthen school culture, support their peers and drive positive change. Through leading initiatives and collaborating with others, students develop confidence, responsibility and empathy — essential skills that prepare them for real world success beyond the classroom.
Students join the JLT through a formal interview and selection process, putting themselves forward as role models who want to make a meaningful difference within the Academy community.
Leadership Through Our Values
The JLT embodies the Academy’s core values of Responsibility, Resilience, Resourcefulness, and Respect. These values underpin everything our student leaders do:
Through open discussion, decision-making, and collaborative projects, JLT members develop essential skills in communication, critical thinking, and active citizenship – qualities that prepare them for leadership far beyond the classroom.
Taking responsibility for shaping positive change.
Building resilience by tackling real challenges.
Being resourceful in teamwork and problem-solving.
Showing respect for others’ experiences and perspectives.
JLT Committees
To maximise their impact, the Junior Leadership Team is organised into specialist committees, each focusing on a key area of Academy life.
This team champions equality, inclusion, and respect across the school. They lead campaigns, deliver assemblies, and work with staff to ensure that all students, regardless of race, culture, or identity, feel seen, safe, and celebrated.
Responsible for bringing the school together, this group plans charity fundraisers, community events, and cultural celebrations such as Children in Need, Cancer Research Race for Life, and our annual Cultural Diversity Week. They create opportunities for students, staff, and families to connect and contribute to a thriving Academy community.
This team focuses on the holistic wellbeing of students. They promote mental health awareness, kindness campaigns, and initiatives that build emotional resilience. Their work helps sustain a nurturing environment where every student can flourish.
Supporting LGBTQ+ students and allies, this group advocates for equality, understanding, and visibility. Through awareness events and community education, they help ensure Hammersmith Academy remains a place where everyone can express their identity and feel proud of who they are.
This group gives students a voice in shaping how they learn. They collaborate with staff to share insights and feedback, helping to make lessons engaging, challenging, and effective for all. Their work strengthens teaching practice and student engagement across the Academy.
Leadership, Service and Character
Leadership and service play a key role in enrichment at Hammersmith Academy.
Students are encouraged to take on roles of responsibility and contribute positively to the wider community.
Our Junior Leadership Team (JLT) leads by example, participating in the TimeGivers initiative and volunteering at a local care home – connecting with older residents, learning from their life experiences, and giving back to the community.
These experiences foster empathy, respect and the sense of civic responsibility that underpin our values.
A Community of Budding Citizens
Hammersmith Academy provides the conditions for students to grow into confident, thoughtful young citizens. The JLT helps nurture a safe and inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and respected. By working together, students learn the importance of empathy, integrity, and civic responsibility – building a community rooted in trust, belonging, and mutual respect.

pageCache.pageTitle: Continued Upward Trajectory for GCSE, A Level and BTEC Results - Hammersmith Academy
pageCache.text:
Continued Upward Trajectory for GCSE, A Level and BTEC Results
Hammersmith Academy is celebrating another year of strong results across GCSE, A Level and BTEC, with students continuing to make exceptional academic progress and Sixth Form performance rising across every headline A Level grade measure.
At GCSE, students placed the Academy in the top 10% nationally for value added, rising from the top 15% last year. This year, 80% of all GCSE grades were awarded at 9–4, with 66% at 9–5 and 27% at the highest grades of 9–7. In the core subjects of both English and Maths, 65% of students achieved grades 9–5.
The results are particularly significant given Hammersmith Academy’s fair-banded admissions, which ensure the Academy admits students across the full range of academic ability. Despite these varied starting points, the Academy ranks in the top 10% nationally for value added across every prior attainment group, as well as for disadvantaged students, and both girls and boys.
Put simply, this means that this year, students at Hammersmith Academy achieved, on average, at least one grade higher in all subjects than their starting points would predict.
Standout GCSE performances were seen across the breadth of the curriculum. In the Sciences, 100% of Physics grades and 80% of Biology and Chemistry grades were awarded at 9–4, while Media, Drama, Art, History and Combined Science all achieved at least 75% at 9–4. Further highlights included 80% of Spanish and 60% of Maths grades at 9–5, while 43% of English Literature grades were awarded at 9–7.
Sixth Form Results Continue to Rise
The upward trajectory continues into Hammersmith Academy Sixth Form, where A Level performance rose across every headline grade measure and students secured places at leading universities including Cambridge, Edinburgh, Warwick, Bath, Imperial and King’s College London, alongside increasingly desirable and competitive apprenticeships including BAE Systems, British Airways, Deutsche Bank, Constructions Logistics Group and Ofcom.
This year, the overall A*–E pass rate reached 100%, with 80% of grades awarded at A*–C, 56% at A*–B and 21% at A*–A.
The results build on the Academy’s strong Sixth Form performance, with A*–C grades rising to 80% from 73% last year, A*–B grades increasing from 51% to 56%, and A*–A grades rising from 20% to 21%.
There were exceptional performances across a broad range of subjects, with 100% of grades in both Spanish and Media awarded at A*–B, alongside 87% in Sociology, 83% in Psychology and 75% in Economics.
At the very highest level, 40% of Spanish grades and 38% of Psychology grades were awarded at A*–A, while 33% of grades in Maths, Further Maths and Sociology achieved the same top grades.
Students on vocational and mixed pathways also achieved outstanding outcomes, with 96% at Distinction*–Merit and 60% at Distinction*–Distinction. Business achieved 100% Distinction*–Merit, with 68% at Distinction*–Distinction, while Sport and Applied Science achieved 80% Distinction*–Distinction.
From Results to Real World Success
Together, the results demonstrate strong performance across the breadth of the Academy, from students making exceptional progress at GCSE to rising A Level results and outstanding vocational outcomes.
They also provide the foundation for students’ next steps. Sixth Form students are progressing to leading universities including Cambridge, Edinburgh, Warwick, Bath, Imperial and King’s College London, while others are pursuing competitive apprenticeship opportunities with BAE Systems, British Airways, Deutsche Bank, Constructions Logistics Group and Ofcom.
Whether students choose an academic or vocational pathway, Hammersmith Academy has the expertise and opportunities to help them achieve real world success. The Academy has invested significantly in specialist Careers and University support, with two dedicated experts providing personalised guidance alongside university visits, employer encounters, careers workshops and an extensive network of partners, preparing students for ambitious next steps.
Headteacher, Gary Kynaston, said:
“These results reflect the hard work and ambition of our students and the dedication of our staff. From students making exceptional progress at GCSE to rising A Level results and strong vocational outcomes, we are delighted to see continued progress across the Academy.
“As a fair-banded school, we educate students from across the full range of academic starting points, so to rank in the top 10% nationally for value added, with students achieving on average at least one grade higher in all subjects than their starting points would predict, is something we are extremely proud of.
“We are equally proud of the breadth of our curriculum and the strong results across core, academic, creative and vocational subjects. Every student has different strengths and talents, and it is important that our curriculum gives them the opportunity to discover, develop and excel in them.
“Ultimately, these results are about where they enable our students to go next. Whether that is university, an apprenticeship or another pathway, our ambition is for every student to leave Hammersmith Academy with the knowledge, confidence and opportunities to achieve real world success.”

School Meals
School Meals
A healthy, balanced diet plays a vital role in helping students learn effectively, stay focused and achieve their very best – both inside and outside the classroom.
At Hammersmith Academy, all students eat Academy-provided meals. We do not allow packed lunches.
This is a deliberate and important choice. We believe that shared, nutritious meals are a powerful leveller, ensuring that every student, regardless of background, starts the day and learns on equal footing. Alongside our mobile phone-free school day, this approach creates calm, focused routines that support wellbeing, concentration and positive social interaction.
A key part of this culture is that staff and students dine together in the canteen each day. This creates a positive community dining experience where conversation, courtesy and strong relationships are encouraged, helping to strengthen the sense of belonging across the Academy.
This approach allows us to:
Our catering is provided by Innovate, a leading school food provider committed to delivering fresh, nutritious meals every day. Our menus are designed to support energy, concentration, and wellbeing, giving students the fuel they need to thrive.
Freshly Prepared Meals
Our catering is provided by Innovate, a leading school food provider committed to delivering fresh, nutritious meals every day. Our menus are designed to support energy, concentration, and wellbeing, giving students the fuel they need to thrive.
All food is prepared daily on-site by the Innovate team, using high-quality ingredients and seasonal produce. Each term features a three-week rotational menu that offers variety, balance and choice, while meeting all dietary and cultural requirements.
Fresh fruit is available every day at breakfast, lunch, and break time. We do not sell sugary snacks or fizzy drinks – helping students make healthy choices that sustain energy throughout the day.
Please see our latest menus for current meal options and allergen information.
Free Breakfast at the Academy
We believe every student deserves the best possible start to their day. Research consistently shows that eating breakfast improves concentration, memory, and academic performance.
To help students begin each day ready to learn, we offer a free porridge breakfast in the cafeteria every morning, with additional healthy breakfast options available at a reduced cost.
Free School Meals
Students who are eligible for Free School Meals (FSM) receive the same high-quality hot lunch from the school menu.
Students may be entitled to Free School Meals (FSM) if parents or carers receive any of the following:
Income-related Employment and Support Allowance
Support under Part VI of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999
The guaranteed element of Pension Credit
Child Tax Credit (without Working Tax Credit and with an income under £16,190)
Children who receive qualifying benefits directly are also eligible. Families with no recourse to public funds may still qualify – please contact the Academy or your local authority for advice.
To check whether you are eligible and to apply for Free School Meals, please click here.
Please note: If your child received Free School Meals at primary school, this does not automatically transfer to secondary school. Parents and carers must provide evidence of eligibility, including a confirmation letter from your local authority, to the Academy’s Finance Department in order to continue receiving Free School Meals.
Income Support

Income-related Employment and Support Allowance
The guaranteed element of Pension Credit
Supporting Healthy Habits for Life
At Hammersmith Academy we help students build healthy habits that support wellbeing, focus, and long-term achievement.
Through our partnership with Innovate, we ensure that every student enjoys food that is fresh, balanced, and made to inspire confidence and success in every aspect of school life.

Uniform

Dressing for Success
At Hammersmith Academy, we believe that presentation is key to success – both in school and in life.
Uniform represents our shared values of respect and responsibility. It unites students in a common identity, builds confidence, and reinforces the importance of high standards in every aspect of Academy life, whilst preparing students for the expectations of the professional world.
Uniform Expectations
The wearing of the Academy uniform is strictly enforced. We ask that all parents support us in maintaining a positive, professional image and upholding the Academy’s reputation for excellence.
All students – apart from Sixth Form, who follow a relaxed business wear dress code – are required to wear full uniform at all times, as outlined below:
Year 7-11
Plain black leather shoes (closed toe, not canvas or suede).
Lace-up shoes permitted; boots (including Kickers or Timberland styles) are not acceptable.
Shoes must be plain, without visible branding, and below ankle height.
No jewellery except a plain watch and one small, discreet metal ear stud in each ear.
No other visible piercings (including nose piercings).
Hair should be worn in a business-appropriate style (plaited or tied back if long).
Extreme hairstyles, colours, or accessories are not permitted.
No make-up or nail polish (except for Sixth Form).
Headscarves and hijabs must be plain black or grey.
Coats must be plain black with no logos or branding.
All hats, scarves, and gloves must be removed before entering the building.
All students are required to use the official Hammersmith Academy bag and PE kit bag.
All students must wear the official Hammersmith Academy PE kit, available from School Uniform Direct:
Non-marking soled training shoes
Academy Fitness T-shirt
Academy Multi-sport Top
Academy Sports Socks
Grey Academy Suit Jacket
Grey Trousers / Tartan Pleated Skirt
Academy Tie
Plain Black Shoes
Sixth Form Dress Code
Sixth Form students are not required to wear uniform but are expected to follow a relaxed business wear dress code.
This means dressing smartly and appropriately for a professional environment while allowing for individuality and comfort.
The standard reflects the maturity of our Sixth Formers and prepares them for the expectations of university and the workplace.
Our Uniform Supplier
All official Hammersmith Academy uniform items are available from our supplier, School Uniform Direct.
Parents can order online via the School Uniform Direct website or visit their local store, which you can find here.
The uniform is designed for comfort, durability, and professionalism, ensuring students look smart and feel confident throughout the day.
Pre-Loved Uniform
We are committed to sustainability and affordability. Parents wishing to purchase or donate pre-loved uniform items can do so through the following platforms:
School Clothing Allowance (Hammersmith & Fulham)
Parents and carers who live within the London Borough of Hammersmith & Fulham may be eligible for a School Clothing Grant to help with the cost of purchasing uniform.
The grant, worth £79, is available for children aged 11 or 14 before 1st September of the current academic year.
If you think your child may be eligible, please complete the online application form available through the borough’s website.
Professional Standards Every Day
Our uniform policy helps build confidence, self-respect, and a sense of unity among students, preparing them for the discipline and presentation standards expected in higher education and the workplace.
All final judgements on acceptability are made by Academy staff. We thank parents and carers for their continued support in upholding our high standards.

pageCache.pageTitle: Secretary of State Visits Hammersmith Academy to Discuss Online Safety - Hammersmith Academy
pageCache.text:
Secretary of State Visits Hammersmith Academy to Discuss Online Safety
Hammersmith Academy was pleased to welcome Liz Kendall, Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, on Thursday 21st May 2026 as part of a visit focused on online safety and young people’s experiences of the digital world.
The visit formed part of the Government’s national consultation, Growing Up in the Online World, which is gathering views from children, parents, schools and communities on the impact of digital technology and social media on young people.
During her visit, the Secretary of State met with students, parents, pastoral staff and Headteacher Gary Kynaston to discuss the opportunities and challenges presented by life online. Conversations explored topics including social media, online wellbeing, digital habits and the role that schools and families play in supporting young people to navigate the online world safely and responsibly.
The Secretary of State also toured the Academy, visiting science lessons and learning more about the school’s approach to supporting student wellbeing and maintaining a focused learning environment. Discussions included Hammersmith Academy’s mobile phone policy, which uses locking pouches to ensure mobile phones remain inaccessible during the school day.
As part of the visit, the Secretary of State also sat down with Channel 4 News for an interview focused on online safety and the Government’s consultation.
Gary Kynaston, Headteacher, said:
“We were delighted to welcome Liz Kendall and representatives from the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology to Hammersmith Academy. Online safety and digital wellbeing are hugely important issues for schools, parents and young people alike. It was invaluable for our students and families to have the opportunity to share their experiences directly and contribute to a national conversation that will help shape future policy.”
The visit reflects Hammersmith Academy’s commitment to preparing students for real world success by helping them develop not only academically, but also the confidence, awareness and resilience needed to navigate modern life safely, responsibly and thoughtfully.
